# Function

## FnInterval.kt { #fninterval-kt }

Certified bounds for an `Fn` over an interval — the third walker of [`FnFormulas`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnformulas), in interval
arithmetic, and what turns a sampled envelope into a guarantee.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
with(Functions) {
    val f = sin(0.025, amplitude = 0.2, offset = 0.45) + gaussian(1234.57, 0.002, 0.5, 0.0..3600.0)
    f.enclose(1234.0, 1235.0)          // lo..hi that every f(x) on that interval lies inside
    f.certifiedRange(0.0, 3600.0)      // the global max, with the x that reaches it
    f.certifiedEnvelope(0.0, 3600.0, 1000)  // per-bin bounds a plot cannot slip between
}
```

### What a sampled envelope cannot say

`SignalViewer` bins a function by evaluating it on a grid and keeping each bin's min and max. A
feature narrower than the grid spacing can sit between two samples and never be drawn, and nothing
in the picture says so. `public/docs/function_conversation.md` states that limit in as many words.
An enclosure is a different kind of object: `[lo, hi]` such that **every** value the function
takes on the interval lies inside, whether or not any sample landed near it. A spike 10 ms wide
in an hour-long signal cannot hide from it, because nothing is sampled.

### One declaration, three walkers

`evalFormulaInterval` walks the same [`FnExpr`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnexpr) tree that `evalFormula` walks in `Double` and
`evalFormulaAD` in tracked arithmetic, so the enclosure is of the function `Fn.eval` computes and
not of a third transcription of it. There is still no per-op code: every op with an [`FnFormulas`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnformulas)
entry is enclosed, and an op without one is **refused by name** (`FnEnclosure.refusal`) — never
bounded by a guess. Most of the hand-written `fn { x -> … }` lambdas in the wild are therefore
refused; that is the cost of a guarantee, and giving an op a formula is how to lift it (it gains
an exact gradient at the same time).

### What exactly is contained

The contract is the **`Double` values `Fn.eval` returns** for every double `x` in `[a, b]` — the
values a sampler draws — not the real-number function those doubles approximate. That choice is
what lets most of the arithmetic go unwidened:

- `+ − × ÷` are correctly rounded, and round-to-nearest is **monotone**, so evaluating an
  interval's endpoints (or a product's four corners) in ordinary `Double` already brackets every
  rounded result in between. No outward rounding is needed, which is why a held constant certifies
  as exactly `[1, 1]` rather than as `1 ± ulp`.
- `abs`, `floor`, `min`, `max`, `coerceIn` and the branch kinds are exact.
- The library transcendentals (`sin`, `exp`, `pow`, `tanh`, `atan2`, …) are *not* correctly
  rounded: the Javadoc allows up to 1–2.5 ulps, and promises only that they are semi-monotonic.
  Their endpoint values are widened outward by `TRANSCENDENTAL_ULPS` ulps each side, which also
  absorbs the rare last-bit disagreement between an interpreted and a JIT-intrinsic `Math.sin`.

NaN is tracked separately (`FnRange.maybeNaN`) rather than widened into the range: `log` of a
range reaching below zero *may* produce NaN, and saying so is more useful than an infinite bound.

### Tightness and branch-and-bound

Plain interval arithmetic is sound but loose: `x - x` over `[0, 1]` encloses as `[-1, 1]`, because
the walker does not know the two `x`s are the same number (the *dependency problem*). The bound
converges to the true range as the interval shrinks, so everything above `Functions.Fn.enclose`
works by subdividing: `certifiedRange` is a best-first branch-and-bound on the maximum and the
minimum, the `certified…` predicates split until each piece is decided, and `certifiedEnvelope`
refines each bin until its bound is within a tolerance of what that bin's samples show.
`FnIntervalTest` measures how loose the one-shot bound is and ratchets the number.

### FnIntervalRefusal { #fninterval-kt-fnintervalrefusal }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FnIntervalRefusal</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">message</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RuntimeException</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">message</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FnInterval/#L125)

Thrown inside a walk when a bound cannot honestly be given — an op with no formula, an unbounded shape domain, a `clamp` whose range may invert (which throws in `Fn.eval` itself). Caught by `FnIntervals.enclose` and reported as `FnEnclosure.refusal`.

## FnMetric.kt { #fnmetric-kt }

The objective shared by both halves of the function-search family: [`FnMetric`](function.md#fnmetric-kt-fnmetric), a `fun interface`
scoring a candidate signal against a target on one even sample grid (lower is better), plus a
companion of ready-made metrics — `rmse`, `mae`, `lp`, `maxError`, `huber`, `logCosh`,
`correlation` — and the `fromResidual` / `window` builders behind them.

`FnMetric.lossAgainst` turns a metric into the `(Fn) -> Double` closure the gradient fitters in
FunctionFit.kt descend, sampling the target once and reusing it across the finite-difference
inner loop; the same metrics are what `matchFitness` in FunctionEvolve.kt negates, so structural
search and numeric fitting can run under one notion of "close". Any metric — including a
hand-written lambda — must ignore indices where either side is non-finite and return
`Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY` when no index is jointly finite, which callers read as maximally bad.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FnMetric.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FnMetric/)

### FnMetric { #fnmetric-kt-fnmetric }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">FnMetric</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FnMetric/#L49)

A pluggable distance metric between a target signal and a candidate, evaluated on a shared even sample grid. **Lower is better**; `0.0` means the candidate matches the target at every sampled point. This is the objective the differentiable fitters (`fitGradient`, `fitBest`, `fitHybrid`) descend; `rmse` is the default and one metric among the family.

## FunctionEvolve.kt { #functionevolve-kt }

Search over the *structure* of `Fn` graphs — the genetic counterpart to the gradient fitting of
a fixed structure's numbers in FunctionFit.kt.

[`FnMutations`](function.md#functionevolve-kt-fnmutations) holds the seeded mutation operators (jitter and nudge numeric leaves, transmute an
op within its `OpRegistry` family, prune, duplicate or graft a subtree), each expressed over the
graph copy and query primitives rather than a private traversal. `evolve` runs them as a bounded
(µ+λ) hill-climb and returns an [`FnEvolveRun`](function.md#functionevolve-kt-fnevolverun) listing every accepted improvement. Fitness is the
caller's: `matchFitness` scores closeness to a target under any `FnMetric`, less an optional
complexity penalty from `graphMetrics`; `noveltyFitness` instead scores distance from an archive
of [`FnBehaviour`](function.md#functionevolve-kt-fnbehaviour) descriptors — what a graph *does* when sampled, not how it is built — and
`evolveVariety` chains slots of novelty search into a behaviourally spread set of results rather
than one best match.

Both runners are bounded by an iteration count so a search cannot disappear into an animation
loop, and both are deterministic: traversal is stable and every draw comes from one seeded
`Random`, with each `evolveVariety` slot deriving `rngSeed * 31 + slot`. Set `normalize` on
`Functions.Fn.behaviour` (and hence on novelty search) to compare shape rather than amplitude.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionEvolve.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionEvolve/)

## FunctionFit.kt { #functionfit-kt }

Gradient-based fitting of `Fn` graphs — the differentiable counterpart to the genetic
`evolve` in FunctionEvolve.kt.

Where `evolve` searches over *structure* (seeded mutation of the graph), this file tunes
the *numbers*: the numeric leaves of a fixed-structure graph are the θ-vector, and Adam
descends the RMSE loss against a target `Fn`. The two are complementary — `fitHybrid`
runs `evolve` to discover a shape, then polishes its constants here.

A lone `fitGradient` is *local* and will stall in a frequency local-minimum when the seed's
oscillator frequencies are far from the target's (RMSE-vs-frequency is periodic, not convex);
`fitBest` wraps it in deterministic jittered restarts and is the entry to reach for when the
starting numbers may be wrong; its own KDoc has the shape of that landscape.

The θ extract/apply primitives ride on `Functions.Fn.mapGraphNumbers`, whose post-order
DFS is stable and deterministic with `preserveSharing = false`: the *i*-th numeric leaf
seen while reading is the *i*-th leaf written while applying, so a plain index counter is
a sound θ↔graph bijection. Everything is deterministic given a seed: Adam itself has no
randomness, and only an optional [`FnFitConfig`](function.md#functionfit-kt-fnfitconfig) init-jitter draws from a single `Random`, so a
fit re-run with the same seed comes back identical. [`FnEvolveRun`](function.md#functionevolve-kt-fnevolverun) holds to the same rule.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionFit.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionFit/)

**Used in:** [Differentiating Functions](../autodiff_examples.md), [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md), [Patterns: writing rhythm as a function of time](../pattern_language.md)

## FunctionGraph.kt { #functiongraph-kt }

The data model and the copy engine underneath Field's graph-rewritable notion of a function:
[`FnGraphNode`](function.md#functiongraph-kt-fngraphnode) / [`FnGraphEdge`](function.md#functiongraph-kt-fngraphedge) (an op name, role-tagged children, scalar metadata and an
optional rebuild recipe) plus `Functions.Fn.deepCopy` and `Functions.Fn.rewriteGraph`, a
bottom-up copy that offers every occurrence to an [`FnGraphEdit`](function.md#functiongraph-kt-fngraphedit). Every other file in this
family runs on that single traversal, as do the edit primitives declared here —
`Functions.Fn.mapGraphNumbers`, `Functions.Fn.replaceOps`, `Functions.Fn.pruneWhere`,
`Functions.Fn.graftWhere`, `Functions.Fn.duplicateWhere`, `Functions.Fn.slideCopy`. The
read-only renderings live here too: `Functions.Fn.graphSnapshot`, `Functions.Fn.graphText`,
`Functions.Fn.graphSvg` and `Functions.Fn.graphFLineMap`.

Two constraints show up everywhere downstream. A node whose `rebuild` is null cannot be
reconstructed, so a copy keeps the original evaluator and drops the recipe. And
`preserveSharing` decides whether a shared subgraph stays shared (memoized by identity) or is
expanded into a tree — `Functions.Fn.deepCopy` defaults it to true, while the rewriting entry
points default it to false so each occurrence can be edited independently.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraph.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraph/)

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md), [Patterns: writing rhythm as a function of time](../pattern_language.md)

## FunctionGraphBrowser.kt { #functiongraphbrowser-kt }

The looking-at-it layer for the `Fn` graph family: sample a graph on one shared time-base, then
render it as a self-contained interactive HTML browser.

`Functions.Fn.graphTrace` samples every visible occurrence three ways — `local` (that subgraph
alone), `muted` (the whole root with the occurrence replaced by a neutral constant: `0.0`, or
`1.0` for a divisor) and `effect` (`final - muted`) — plus optional value sweeps for numeric
nodes, and `Functions.Fn.graphBrowseHtml` / `Functions.Fn.browseGraph` wrap that in a canvas UI.
`Functions.Fn.graphRewriteTrace` is the same idea for rewriting: it applies rules cumulatively
— either `FnGraphRule`s or the meaningful lines of a string-DSL spec — recording before, after
and delta per stage for `FnRewriteTrace.rewriteBrowseHtml` and `Functions.Fn.browseRewrite`.

`effect` is a counterfactual, not an additive decomposition: it includes every transformation
between the occurrence and the root. Tracing is bounded by `maxDepth`/`maxNodes` and sampling is
NaN-safe (out-of-domain and throwing evaluations become `NaN` and are simply left undrawn). The
`browse*` functions display into the current box and throw without an active `Box.context`; the
`*Html` functions are pure strings and work anywhere.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphBrowser.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphBrowser/)

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md)

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FnGraphSweepPoint</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">samples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphBrowser/#L27)

One swept value of a numeric node and the final signal it produces.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | The value substituted at the swept node — the node is replaced by a plain constant holding it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">samples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The *whole root* sampled with that substitution in place, on the trace's shared abscissae. |

One occurrence of the graph, sampled three ways on the root's time-base — and, if it is a number and you asked for sweeps, once more per swept value.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">path</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Child indices from the root; empty is the root itself, which the trace does include. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">role</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The role of the edge this occurrence hangs from, or null at the root. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">op</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The op name, as the sidebar labels it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The occurrence's own function name, if it had one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">domain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Domain</span></code> | The occurrence's own domain, which can be narrower than the domain actually plotted. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">local</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | This subgraph sampled directly at the root's abscissae, ignoring everything above it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">muted</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The rebuilt root with just this occurrence replaced by a neutral constant — `0.0`, or `1.0` when it is the right-hand side of a divide. Muting the root itself therefore flatlines the whole trace. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">effect</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | `final - muted`, index by index, and non-finite wherever either side was. The contextual effect. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">numeric</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | True when this node carries a numeric `value` and is tagged as a number — the sweepable nodes. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | That numeric value, or null for anything else. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sensitivity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FnGraphSweepPoint</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The value sweep behind the browser's sensitivity view. Empty unless the node is `numeric` *and* the caller asked for `sensitivitySteps` above zero — the trace does not sweep by default, though `Functions.Fn.graphBrowseHtml` does. |

### FnGraphTrace { #functiongraphbrowser-kt-fngraphtrace }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FnGraphTrace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">domain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Domain</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">final</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nodes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FnGraphTraceNode</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphBrowser/#L86)

A whole graph sampled on one shared time-base: the abscissae, the finished signal, and one [`FnGraphTraceNode`](function.md#functiongraphbrowser-kt-fngraphtracenode) per visible occurrence.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">domain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Domain</span></code> | The domain actually plotted, after an infinite or empty one was widened into something finite. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The shared abscissae every array in the trace is indexed by. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">final</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The unmodified root sampled at `xs` — the gray curve the browser always keeps on screen. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nodes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FnGraphTraceNode</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | One entry per sampled occurrence, root first. |

### FnRewriteStage { #functiongraphbrowser-kt-fnrewritestage }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FnRewriteStage</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">before</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">after</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">delta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">changed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphBrowser/#L179)

One rewrite step: the signal before and after applying a single rule, on the shared axis.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | What the step is called: the rule's name, or the raw spec line for the string-DSL form. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">before</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The signal as it stood before this rule — i.e. after every earlier stage, since they accumulate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">after</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The signal after this rule. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">delta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | `after - before`, non-finite wherever either side was. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">changed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether the rule really changed the graph, judged structurally rather than by the samples — a rule that matched nothing, or whose transmutation was refused, reports false and the stepper labels it `no-op`. A structural change with a flat `delta` is perfectly possible, and interesting. |

### FnRewriteTrace { #functiongraphbrowser-kt-fnrewritetrace }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FnRewriteTrace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">domain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Domain</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">original</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">finalSamples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stages</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FnRewriteStage</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphBrowser/#L204)

A rewrite watched one rule at a time: the shared abscissae, the signal before anything ran, the signal at the end, and a [`FnRewriteStage`](function.md#functiongraphbrowser-kt-fnrewritestage) per rule.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">domain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Domain</span></code> | The domain actually plotted, after an infinite or empty one was widened into something finite. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The shared abscissae every array here is indexed by. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">original</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The receiver sampled before any rule ran. |

## FunctionGraphRules.kt { #functiongraphrules-kt }

The query and rule-runner layer over the graph copier in FunctionGraph.kt.

Queries come first, and none of them copy or evaluate the function:
`Functions.Fn.graphMatches` and `Functions.Fn.firstGraphMatch` visit a shared node once per
incoming path, so role, ancestry, depth and path stay meaningful for editing;
`Functions.Fn.graphMetrics` separates unique DAG nodes from occurrences and charges a
caller-supplied cost; `Functions.Fn.graphSignature` reduces structure to a deterministic string
with evaluator closures and rebuild lambdas excluded. On top of those, [`FnGraphRule`](function.md#functiongraphrules-kt-fngraphrule)
pairs a named predicate with a replacement, and `Functions.Fn.rewriteWithRules` (one bottom-up
pass) and `Functions.Fn.rewriteUntilStable` (repeated passes) apply them, returning an
[`FnGraphRewriteRun`](function.md#functiongraphrules-kt-fngraphrewriterun) that records every edit that actually changed a node's signature.

Fixed-point rewriting is bounded: `Functions.Fn.rewriteUntilStable` compares
signatures each pass and reports `FnGraphRewriteStop.STABLE`, `FnGraphRewriteStop.CYCLE` or
`FnGraphRewriteStop.MAX_PASSES` rather than letting a non-terminating rule set hide inside an
animation loop. Rules default to `FnGraphRuleMode.FIRST_MATCH` at each node, so ordering is
explicit; `FnGraphRuleMode.ALL_MATCHES` chains every matching rule on the same copy.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphRules.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphRules/)

## FunctionOps.kt { #functionops-kt }

The op vocabulary for the whole `Fn` graph family, held in one object, [`OpRegistry`](function.md#functionops-kt-opregistry): which op
names the stdlib actually emits into a graph node, which of them are aliases of each other, and
which can be rebuilt from an arbitrary node's role-addressed children — those rebuildable ones
each carrying a family label (oscillator, noise, transform, …).

Everything that has to reason about ops consults it instead of keeping a private list — the
rewrite DSL's `op=` validator and its hint text, the pattern matcher's alias-aware op
comparison, `rebuildAsOp`, and the "another op in the same family" draw behind the
`substituteOp` mutation. The Monaco `fnrewrite.js` extension mirrors it, and a JVM test asserts
that mirror never drifts.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionOps.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionOps/)

## FunctionRewriteDsl.kt { #functionrewritedsl-kt }

The `selector => action` string rewrite DSL, compiled and applied end to end.
`compileFnRewrite` parses a spec into an [`FnRewriteProgram`](function.md#functionrewritedsl-kt-fnrewriteprogram) carrying line/column
[`FnRewriteDiagnostic`](function.md#functionrewritedsl-kt-fnrewritediagnostic)s; `Functions.Fn.rewrite`, `Functions.Fn.previewRewrite` (which also
reports match paths and which rules did nothing) and `Functions.Fn.rewriteChecked` (which
refuses an invalid program) run it over the graph copier. Selector matching lives here — op,
role, name, tag and depth tokens, `parent=`, `[key>=n]` predicates and slash-separated path
selectors with `*` and `**` wildcards — and so does action application: `op=`, `name=`,
`domain=`, `drop`, and the numeric `=`, `*=`, `/=`, `+=`, `-=` forms. `op=` targets are checked
against `OpRegistry`; an unknown op is reported as a warning, not an error.

The file does not depend on the live-code compiler. A Kotlin right-hand side is
parsed out of its `@{...}` (or dollar-brace) wrapper and then handed to
`FnRewriteOptions.kotlinNumberContext`; when no caller supplied one, the action is simply not
applied. FunctionRewriteKotlin.kt is what plugs a box's Kotlin engine into that hook, and
FunctionRewritePattern.kt is the separate structural pattern-to-template surface.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewriteDsl.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewriteDsl/)

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md)

## FunctionRewriteKotlin.kt { #functionrewritekotlin-kt }

The bridge that gives the string rewrite DSL a real Kotlin right-hand side.

FunctionRewriteDsl.kt parses `@{...}` expressions but never compiles them; this file supplies
the `FnRewriteOptions.kotlinNumberContext` hook it leaves open, compiling each expression as a
`FnRewriteNumberContext -> Any?` lambda inside a live box's coding context so a snippet can read
`value`, `op`, `parentOp`, `depth` and the rest as plain properties.
[`SourceBackedFnRewriteNumberExpression`](function.md#functionrewritekotlin-kt-sourcebackedfnrewritenumberexpression) stores only source plus a box id and hydrates on first
use; [`SourceBackedFnRewriteNumberEvaluator`](function.md#functionrewritekotlin-kt-sourcebackedfnrewritenumberevaluator) caches one per distinct expression string. The entry
points are `Functions.Fn.rewriteKotlin`, `Functions.Fn.previewRewriteKotlin`,
`Functions.Fn.rewriteKotlinChecked` and the `Box.rewriteFn` / `Box.previewRewriteFn` receiver
forms — each is the corresponding plain-DSL call with that evaluator wired in.

Hydration requires the originating box to still be loaded and the compiled lambda to return a
`Number?`; anything else throws, naming the box or the offending source. When
there is no box in scope no evaluator is installed at all, so Kotlin right-hand sides are left
unapplied; the compiler-free `rewrite(...)` path never needs one.

**Do not call `rewriteKotlin` (or `thisBox.rewriteFn`) from the body of the box the snippets compile
in.** Hydration evaluates on that box's own engine, which re-instantiates its snippet chain and so
re-runs the body that is already running — once per matched node, until the stack goes. It is guarded
now: the second hydration for a box on one thread throws [`FnRewriteSelfBoxReentry`](function.md#functionrewritekotlin-kt-fnrewriteselfboxreentry), whose message
names the ways out. Same hazard as `afield.stdlib.SourceBackedBlock`, reached by a second route; see
`dev_docs/FN_REWRITE_SELF_BOX_REENTRY.md`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewriteKotlin.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewriteKotlin/)

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md)

### FnRewriteSelfBoxReentry { #functionrewritekotlin-kt-fnrewriteselfboxreentry }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FnRewriteSelfBoxReentry</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">box</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">source</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">IllegalStateException</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;This rewrite is compiling '@{$source}' in box '${box.name}' (${box.id}) — the box that is running it, &quot;</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="s">&quot;whose body it therefore re-runs, once per matched node, until the stack overflows. &quot;</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="s">&quot;Run the rewrite somewhere that is not this box's own body: &quot;</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="s">&quot;(1) from another box — &#96;other.rewriteFn(fn, spec)&#96;, e.g. &#96;parents.last().rewriteFn(fn, spec)&#96;, &quot;</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="s">&quot;where &#96;other&#96; is idle; &quot;</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="s">&quot;(2) from a frame loop or a control callback, after this body has finished; or &quot;</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="s">&quot;(3) with a typed evaluator instead of a source string — &#96;fnRewriteNumber { value &#42; 2.0 }&#96; &quot;</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="s">&quot;carries a live lambda and never compiles anything. &quot;</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="s">&quot;See dev&#95;docs/FN&#95;REWRITE&#95;SELF&#95;BOX&#95;REENTRY.md.&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewriteKotlin/#L53)

Thrown when a `@{...}` right-hand side would be compiled in a box whose body is already running — the failure that used to be 172 nested body runs and a `StackOverflowError`. The in-flight set it consults is `afield.stdlib.hydratingBoxes`, shared with `SourceBackedBlock`'s identical guard.

### SourceBackedFnRewriteNumberExpression { #functionrewritekotlin-kt-sourcebackedfnrewritenumberexpression }

## FunctionRewritePattern.kt { #functionrewritepattern-kt }

The third rewriting surface in the family, and the algebraic one. FunctionRewriteDsl.kt is
`selector => action` and edits one matched node in place; `FnGraphRule` in FunctionGraphRules.kt
is a hand-written predicate plus a hand-written replacement; here both sides of a rule are graph
shapes with metavariables ([`FnPattern`](function.md#functionrewritepattern-kt-fnpattern)), so `add(?x, 0) => ?x` reads as an identity rather than
an instruction. `fnRule` compiles a spec into an ordinary `FnGraphRule`, which is what lets
pattern rules reuse the existing traced, bounded, cycle-detecting runners;
`Functions.Fn.rewritePatterns` is the fixed-point convenience over a set of specs.

Matching and the parser are both here. A `?name` binds a subtree and, if repeated, must bind a
structurally equal one (compared by `graphSignature()`); a bare number matches a numeric node's
`value` to within 1e-12; op names are compared through `OpRegistry`'s alias table; `op(a, b, …)`
constrains only the leading children. The string template side is narrower than the pattern
side: a bare op transmutes the matched node, only add/subtract/multiply/divide accept an
explicit child list, and any other `op(...)` template throws — the `fnRule` overload taking a
Kotlin builder over [`FnPatternMatch`](function.md#functionrewritepattern-kt-fnpatternmatch) is the general escape.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewritePattern.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewritePattern/)

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md)

## autodiff_fn.kt { #autodiff-fn-kt }

Differentiating the `Fn` graph itself — the bridge from `autodiff.kt`'s scalar tape to the
graphs `Functions` builds.

`Functions.Fn` is a closure over `Double`, so it cannot be differentiated by overloading its
arithmetic. But every `Fn` the stdlib builds also carries an inspectable [`FnGraphNode`](function.md#functiongraph-kt-fngraphnode): the op
name, the role-tagged children, the scalar metadata. This file **re-interprets that structure in
[`AD`](math.md#autodiff-kt-ad) arithmetic**, so the exact derivative of a graph's output with respect to its numeric leaves
— the same θ-vector `extractParameters` reads and `applyParameters` writes — falls out of one
backward sweep instead of `2n` extra evaluations.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
with(Functions) {
    val f = sin(1.5, amplitude = 0.8, offset = 0.2)
    f.gradientAt(0.3)          // d f(0.3) / d theta, exact, in leaf order
}
```

### Which ops, and the agreement check

The interpreter covers the smooth algebraic core — see `FnAutoDiff.differentiableOps`. That is
a *subset*: the piecewise oscillators (`saw`, `square`), the table-backed
interpolants, the noise generators and everything with baked point data are not here, and
`FnAutoDiff.supports` answers correctly for any graph.

A second interpreter can silently compute the derivative of a *different function* from the one
`eval` computes, so the two are compared instead of assumed to match: `FnAutoDiff.agrees`
re-evaluates the interpreter against `Functions.Fn.eval` on the caller's own sample grid and
reports the worst disagreement, and the fitters run that check before switching over. A mismatch
demotes the run to finite differences rather than returning a confident wrong gradient.

### Ops indexed by leaf, not by node

θ-indices are assigned by exactly the traversal `Functions.Fn.mapGraphNumbers` uses — post-order
DFS over `node.children` in order, one index per node carrying `numbers["value"]` — so index *i*
here is the same leaf as index *i* in `extractParameters`. `FnAutoDiff.leafIndices` is that map,
keyed by the child-index path, and a test asserts the two agree leaf for leaf.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/autodiff_fn.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/autodiff_fn/)

**Used in:** [Differentiating Functions](../autodiff_examples.md)

## autodiff_formula.kt { #autodiff-formula-kt }

One declaration of each `Fn` op's pointwise semantics, walked by two evaluators — so `Fn.eval` and
the reverse-mode gradient cannot compute different functions.

### One declaration, two walkers

The per-op formula lives in exactly one place — [`FnFormulas`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnformulas) — as a tiny expression tree
([`FnExpr`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnexpr)) over the op's role-addressed children and the sample position `x`. Two walkers consume
it:

- `evalFormula` in `Double`, transcribed to be **bit-identical** to the hand-written closure in
  `Functions.kt` (same operations, same order, same `Math.pow` / `coerceIn` calls);
- `evalFormulaAD` in tracked [`AD`](math.md#autodiff-kt-ad) arithmetic.

The AD side therefore has **no per-op code at all**. Adding an op means adding one [`FnExpr`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnexpr) and
the gradient follows, so a transcription error has one place to hide per [`FnExpr`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnexpr) kind rather
than one per op.

`AutoDiffFnBridgeTest.theFormulaTableIsABitIdenticalTranscriptionOfFnEval` is what holds the two
walkers together: for every op with a formula it compares the `Double` walker's output to
`Functions`' own `eval` as raw bits (`toRawBits`), over a 129-point grid at three parameter
vectors. A formula that is not a faithful transcription fails in CI.

`FnAutoDiff.agrees` — the runtime value-agreement check the fitters run before switching to
exact gradients — stays as well, because it catches what the table cannot express at all: an
unbounded shape domain, an inverted `clamp` range.

### The cost of the walk

Making the walk the only traversal would take one edit: every op in `Functions` builds its `Fn`
through one private factory, `graphFn(domain, name, op, …, eval: (Double) -> Double)`, so a
formula-derived evaluator could go in there without touching the individual factories.

It is not done because the walk costs several times a closure call, and `Fn.eval` is where that
lands hardest: it is the hottest call in the library, and one `fitGradient` at the defaults is
`200 × (2·leaves + 1) × 128` whole-graph evaluations, with plotting, `FnMetric`, `evolve` and
every sampler on the same path. The cost is the per-node `when` dispatch and the `Child` role
lookup — a linear scan of `node.children` — against a closure the JIT inlines wholesale.
`FnFormulaBenchmarkTest` prints the ratio for three graphs; it asserts only that the two paths
accumulate bit-identical sums, so those timings are a report and not a contract.

The two costs to attack first would be that role lookup (pre-resolve `Child(role)` to a child
index when the formula is built) and the recursive `when` (flatten to a post-order array of
opcodes with a value stack).
